record.paper_title: Selected Old Open Problems in General Topology
record.context_brief: Weakly first-countable compact spaces of large size
record.original_question: A space X is called weakly first-countable if for each x in X there is a decreasing sequence η_x = (V_n(x): n ∈ ω) with x ∈ V_n(x) such that a set U ⊆ X is open exactly when for every x ∈ U there exists n ∈ ω with V_n(x) ⊆ U. Does there exist, in ZFC, a weakly first-countable compact space X with cardinality strictly greater than 2^ω?

evidence.quote:
(wf c) A subset U of X is open if and only if for every x ∈ U there exists n ∈ ω
such that Vn(x) ⊂ U . In this case, we will say that the family {ηx : x ∈ X} is a weakly basic wf c-
structure on the space X. A space X is called weakly ﬁrst-countable if there exists
a weakly basic wf c-structure on X.

Problem 2 (Arhangel’skii, 1966) . Give an example in ZF C of a weakly ﬁrst-
countable compact space X such that |X| > 2
ω.

artifact.status_search_result: The problem, posed by Arhangel'skii in 1966, asks for a ZFC example of a weakly first-countable compact space of cardinality greater than the continuum. Examples of such spaces have been constructed under additional set-theoretic hypotheses such as CH (Jakovlev 1976, Malykhin 1982) and under b = c, but no ZFC example with cardinality strictly greater than 2^ω appears to be verified in the available literature. The status remains unclear from web search.

status_evidence.title: On Jakovlev spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Arhangelskii 1966 asked whether compact weakly first countable spaces are first countable; Jakovlev (1976) gave a negative answer under CH; strengthened by Malykhin (1982) under CH; later constructed under b=c and by forcing.
status_evidence.claim: Constructions of weakly first-countable compact non-first-countable spaces are known under CH and b=c, but ZFC examples of size > 2^ω are not established.

status_evidence.title: Examples of Weakly First-Countable Compact Spaces in ZFC
status_evidence.snippet: Paper addressing problems of Arhangel'skii on weakly first-countable compact spaces in ZFC.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work has examined Arhangel'skii-type problems in ZFC.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A topological space X is called weakly first-countable if to each point x ∈ X one can assign a decreasing sequence η_x = (V_n(x) : n ∈ ω) of subsets of X with x ∈ V_n(x) for every n, such that a subset U ⊆ X is open if and only if for every x ∈ U there exists n ∈ ω with V_n(x) ⊆ U. Let 2^ω denote the cardinality of the continuum. Working in ZFC (Zermelo–Fraenkel set theory with the Axiom of Choice), determine whether there exists a compact Hausdorff weakly first-countable space X such that |X| > 2^ω.
